title: Multiplayer Electron Orbital Probability Cloud
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that renders an interactive multiplayer electron orbital probability cloud visualization for a hydrogen-like atom. The scene must implement the following:

## Scene Setup
- Black background, perspective camera at (0, 0, 40), FOV 60, looking at origin.
- Ambient light (0x404040) and a point light (0xffffff, 1.5) at (20, 20, 20).
- A translucent nucleus sphere at the origin, radius 0.5, color 0xff4444, opacity 0.8.
- OrbitControls for camera rotation (damping enabled).
- A coordinate axes helper of size 8, toggleable via UI.

## Orbital System
- Implement quantum orbital probability clouds for these orbitals: 1s, 2s, 2p_x, 2p_y, 2p_z, 3d_xy.
- Each orbital is rendered as a THREE.Points cloud of exactly 5000 particles.
- Particle positions are sampled from the radial and angular probability distributions of each orbital using the hydrogen wave functions (use Bohr radius a0 = 1.0 as unit).
- For 1s: R(r) ~ r * exp(-r/a0), angular uniform on sphere.
- For 2s: R(r) ~ (2 - r/a0) * r * exp(-r/(2*a0)), angular uniform.
- For 2p_x: R(r) ~ r^2 * exp(-r/(2*a0)), angular ~ sin(theta)*cos(phi).
- For 2p_y: R(r) ~ r^2 * exp(-r/(2*a0)), angular ~ sin(theta)*sin(phi).
- For 2p_z: R(r) ~ r^2 * exp(-r/(2*a0)), angular ~ cos(theta).
- For 3d_xy: R(r) ~ r^3 * exp(-r/(3*a0)), angular ~ sin^2(theta)*sin(2*phi).
- Each orbital has a distinct color: 1s=#00aaff, 2s=#00ff88, 2p_x=#ff6600, 2p_y=#ffcc00, 2p_z=#ff00ff, 3d_xy=#00ffff.
- Particle size = 0.08, with additive blending and depth write off.
- Only one orbital is visible at a time initially (start with 1s).

## Multiplayer Electron System
- Support up to 4 electrons that can be placed into orbitals.
- Each electron is tracked with: id (1-4), orbitalAssignment (string), spinState ('up' or 'down'), energy level (n value).
- Enforce the Pauli Exclusion Principle: no two electrons can share the same orbital AND spin state. If violated, reject the assignment and set window.__3D_STATE__.pauliViolationCount += 1.
- Track total system energy as sum of -13.6/n^2 eV for each assigned electron.
- Display electron assignments in a HUD panel (top-right, semi-transparent dark background).

## User Interactions
- Dropdown select (#orbital-select) to switch visible orbital: options '1s','2s','2p_x','2p_y','2p_z','3d_xy'.
- Button (#add-electron) to add an electron to the currently visible orbital with default spin 'up'. If orbital+spin is occupied, try 'down'. If both occupied, reject.
- Button (#remove-electron) to remove the last added electron (undo-style, LIFO order).
- Button (#redo-electron) to redo the last removed electron (redo stack, cleared on new add).
- Keyboard 'U' toggles spin of the most recently added electron between 'up' and 'down' (re-validate Pauli).
- Keyboard 'R' resets all electrons (clears all assignments, resets energy, resets violation count).
- Keyboard 'T' toggles axes helper visibility.
- Keyboard 'E' toggles an energy level diagram overlay: a DOM div (#energy-diagram) showing horizontal lines for n=1,2,3 with dots for placed electrons.
- Click on the Three.js canvas performs raycasting: if the nucleus is clicked, pulse-animate it (scale 1.0 -> 1.5 -> 1.0 over 0.5s) and set nucleusPulsing=true during animation.

## Superposition Mode
- Button (#superposition-toggle) toggles superposition mode on/off.
- When ON, ALL orbitals that have at least one electron assigned become visible simultaneously (overlaid).
- When OFF, revert to showing only the selected orbital.
- In superposition mode, each orbital cloud slowly rotates around Y axis at rate = 0.1 * n (quantum number) radians/sec.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
- currentOrbital: string (currently selected orbital name)
- visibleOrbitals: array of strings (currently visible orbital names)
- electronCount: number (total assigned electrons, 0-4)
- electrons: array of objects [{id, orbital, spin, energy}]
- totalEnergy: number (sum of electron energies in eV, e.g. -13.6 for one 1s electron)
- pauliViolationCount: number (cumulative rejected assignments)
- superpositionMode: boolean
- nucleusPulsing: boolean
- axesVisible: boolean
- energyDiagramVisible: boolean
- undoStackSize: number (number of electrons that can be redone)
- particleCounts: object mapping orbital name to number of particles currently in scene
- cameraDistance: number (camera distance from origin)
- lastAction: string ('add'|'remove'|'redo'|'spin_toggle'|'reset'|'orbital_switch'|'superposition_toggle'|'none')

## Animation
- Animate at 60fps. Each orbital cloud gently oscillates particle opacity (0.3 to 0.7) using sin(time).
- The nucleus gently bobs up and down by 0.1 units using sin(time * 2).

## HUD
- Top-left: current orbital name, electron count, total energy (eV, 2 decimal places).
- Top-right: electron assignment table.
- Bottom-center: control instructions text.
physics_constraints: Pauli Exclusion Principle must be enforced: no two electrons may occupy the same orbital with the same spin quantum number. Energy levels follow E_n = -13.6/n^2 eV. Total energy is conserved as sum of individual electron energies. Particle distributions must follow hydrogen-like radial probability densities. Undo/redo must maintain consistent state.
